default.text:
I'm so sorry you're going through this. Losing someone you care about, especially without warning, can feel like a deep wound. It's completely valid to feel sad, confused, or even numb right now. These emotions are part of the process, and you don’t have to push them away.

Please know you’re not alone. Many people have walked this path and found their way through the pain. Healing isn’t linear—some days will be harder than others, and that’s okay. Be gentle with yourself. Allow yourself to grieve, cry if you need to, and take small steps toward self-care: rest, eat nourishing food, move your body, and reach out to someone you trust.

If you're open to it, talking to a therapist or counselor can provide a safe space to process your feelings. You don’t have to carry this alone.

And remember: your worth isn’t defined by someone else’s decision. This pain doesn’t mean you’re unlovable—it means you were loved, and that matters. You are worthy of love, care, and a future filled with peace and joy. Keep going. You’re stronger than you know. 💛

care.text:
I'm so sorry you're going through this. Losing someone you care about, especially without warning, can feel incredibly overwhelming and painful. It's completely okay to feel sad, confused, or even numb right now—your emotions are valid.

If you're comfortable, I'm here to listen whenever you want to talk. Sometimes just saying what you're feeling out loud can help. And if you're not ready to talk, that's okay too. You don't have to go through this alone.

In the meantime, be gentle with yourself. Take small, kind actions—rest, eat something nourishing, or do something that brings you a little comfort, even if it's just a quiet moment with a warm drink or a favorite song.

You are not alone, and healing takes time. I'm here for you, whenever you need. 💛
